I've had the same issue since I started with the Blink integration.  Tried removing / re-adding many times on multiple HAAS installs.
Same problem occurs sporadically here. Usually a manual `blink.blink_update` solves the issue for me.

To start- any incomplete image download comes down to the quality of connection between your blink camera/sync module and the Blink servers. You could have blazing fast internet speeds, but the bottle neck is the Blink connection. The app is aware of far more than the integration is. The integration is "dumb" and requires some fiddling on the user side to get things to work right.

A few things I noticed in your automation:
1. You have no delay between the first camera snapshot and the first blink update. There's a wait_for_trigger command in there but with no trigger I doubt there's any delay.
2. Any delays you have are bare minimum of 5s

I do not know how Blink handles things on their side. But what is likely happening is you take the snapshot -> immediately call update. Followed by another update 5s later. Then Blink throttles the calls because of how fast they happened in succession and the data received by the library is corrupted.

I believe the simplest fix here is to call update once after a longer delay. There's an example of this in the documentation but trigger -> delay -> update. That's it. Play with the delay. Try 10s, 30s, etc. If none of those work, step two would be to another delay->update combo after the first delay->update combo. This is just to see if you can get an image fully downloaded.

As an example, see below (this is a script but illustrates the idea)

```yaml
blink_trigger_camera:
  alias: Script - Blink Trigger Camera 
  sequence:
    - service: blink.trigger_camera
      data:
          name: "Camera1"
    - delay: 00:00:10
    - service: blink.blink_update
```  

But keep in mind what @philipp-frank said is true- even with those delays you can still encounter sporadic incomplete downloads as a result of Blink throttling. The App will always be aware of this, but the library will not be. Your best course of action to avoid those problems is just making the delay between requesting a new image and grabbing it with the library (blink_update) as long as you can tolerate.

Like everyone i just reload the blink integration to solve the problem.

I fixed this by setting the scan interval on the integration to 86400 seconds (1 day) and have not had this issue since. I have an automation that updates the cameras every hour, and calls the blink update service every 5 minutes. Haven't noticed any battery drain issues either and I get a full image every time.

Hopefully I didn't break anything :)

EAsy fix is to change the Scan Interval in the Integration configurations. to an absurd high number then create an autmoation that run every X minutes or on presence detection. I just change it to 9999999999 seconds (~ 317 years) and now no more broken thumbnails.

review_comments: Don't copy `None` to string. That is probably not intended.

We don't want to copy None, but user_input.get() throws a lint error because it supposedly can return None.
What is the "right" way to address the lint error? Assert string?
The pin is optional, right? What should we do if the user doesn't enter a pin?

In this case, no pin, or the incorrect pin fails the send pin code directly after `_send_blink_2fa_pin().`
I think we should eliminate the var and put this on the call to _send_blink_2fa_pin as well, the value is only used one time.
If the pin is required for the api, I suggest updating the form schema to make it required.

@MartinHjelmare in theory it's required, but Blink's API is wonky and sometimes a 2fa key is never sent but the user is able to click through and send no key and still set up the platform. That's why it is currently not required in the schema. It feels weird, but that's the historical reason at least.
Does the library accept no pin or passing `None` as pin?
